1.1.1.name: Non-text Content
1.1.1.summary: All non-text content has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.

1.3.1.name: Info and Relationships
1.3.1.summary: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined.

1.3.5.name: Identify Input Purpose
1.3.5.summary: The purpose of each input field collecting user information can be programmatically determined.

1.4.1.name: Use of Color
1.4.1.summary: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information or distinguishing elements.

1.4.2.name: Audio Control
1.4.2.summary: Auto-playing audio longer than 3 seconds can be paused, stopped, or its volume controlled.

1.4.3.name: Contrast (Minimum)
1.4.3.summary: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).

1.4.4.name: Resize Text
1.4.4.summary: Text can be resized up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.

1.4.10.name: Reflow
1.4.10.summary: Content reflows to a single column at 320 CSS pixels without two-dimensional scrolling.

1.4.11.name: Non-text Contrast
1.4.11.summary: UI components and graphical objects have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.

1.4.12.name: Text Spacing
1.4.12.summary: No loss of content when users adjust line height, paragraph, letter, and word spacing.

2.1.1.name: Keyboard
2.1.1.summary: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings.

2.4.1.name: Bypass Blocks
2.4.1.summary: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content repeated on multiple pages.

2.4.2.name: Page Titled
2.4.2.summary: Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose.

2.4.4.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
2.4.4.summary: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text or its context.

2.4.6.name: Headings and Labels
2.4.6.summary: Headings and labels describe topic or purpose.

2.4.7.name: Focus Visible
2.4.7.summary: Any keyboard-operable interface has a mode where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

2.5.3.name: Label in Name
2.5.3.summary: For components with visible text labels, the accessible name contains the visible text.

3.1.1.name: Language of Page
3.1.1.summary: The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined.

3.1.2.name: Language of Parts
3.1.2.summary: The human language of each passage can be programmatically determined.

3.2.2.name: On Input
3.2.2.summary: Changing a setting does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user is advised.

3.3.1.name: Error Identification
3.3.1.summary: Input errors are identified and described to the user in text.

3.3.2.name: Labels or Instructions
3.3.2.summary: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input.

4.1.2.name: Name, Role, Value
4.1.2.summary: For all UI components, the name, role, states, and values can be programmatically determined and set.

4.1.3.name: Status Messages
4.1.3.summary: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties without receiving focus.
